name: Indigo Mastercard
perks: Unsecured card, so no security deposit is required
Prequalification uses a soft pull that does not hurt your credit score
Reports to all three major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion)
Accepts applicants with prior bankruptcy or deep subprime scores
Standard Mastercard acceptance and $0 fraud liability
drawbacks: Annual fee runs up to $175 the first year, then $49 plus $12.50 per month (about $199 per year) on the highest-fee offer, as of mid-2026; exact terms vary by offer and applicant
The fee math is brutal: a $175 first-year fee on a $300 limit consumes 58% of your available credit before you buy anything
Credit limits are typically $300 to $700, and Indigo rarely grants increases
Purchase APR is roughly 24.9% to 35.9% depending on the offer you receive
No rewards, no cash back, no upgrade path to a better card
Issued by Celtic Bank and serviced by Concora Credit, which draws heavy complaint volume over fees and customer service

A no-fee secured card like the Discover it Secured or Capital One Platinum Secured builds credit for $0 a year and refunds your deposit; if you can save even $49 to $200 for a deposit, the secured route is almost always better
Verdict: skip it unless you have zero money for a deposit and were declined by Mission Lane; if you do take it, pay in full monthly and treat it as a 12-month stepping stone
